# R371 — Ryzen 5 5600X AVX2 native expert decode: operation/byte split and next measurements

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only source and external implementation research. Fixed source: `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/diag-native-copy-queue-qualified-20261013`, HEAD `410904c99d273435b5302fa8976cc667d17957f2`. Main's phase-cache/sourceLLVM worktree was not read for conclusions. No source, Git, build, test, GPU, service, or model-run operation was performed. Only this report was created. Pack metadata was read as text; no shard or large binary was read.

## Decision in one paragraph

For this 2560→640 expert, arithmetic per expert-token is fixed across the listed formats: GU is 3,276,800 weight×activation products (640 gate plus 640 up rows), Down is 1,638,400, total 4,915,200 products / 9,830,400 conventional multiply-add FLOPs. Packed GU is 1,049,600–1,408,000 B depending on IQ2_S/IQ3_XXS/IQ3_S; Down is 921,600 B for either IQ4_NL or Q2_0. These extents alone do not identify current DRAM traffic. First read existing per-request/per-phase CPU counters together with the route's actual NT buckets and split by format; then collect matched hot-set and streaming kernel timings, with quantizers separately. The most concrete new source candidate is the NT5–8 Down wrapper re-decoding identical weight blocks in groups of four. Its payoff depends on actual NT5–8 incidence. Do not start with quantization or precision changes.

Line references below are from that worktree. `native_expert.cpp:53-66` computes row sizes, offsets, activation types, and total extent from GGML traits; `:94-155` selects custom AVX2 versus GGML per NT; `:157-176` selects IQ4_NL Down. `iq_avx2_rows.inl:77-102` decodes a weight half once and loops over NT activation vectors. `:203-259` define IQ2_XXS/IQ2_S/IQ3_XXS packed block sizes and decode forms; `:261-315` contain IQ3_S and IQ4_NL row loops; `:224-251` show GU NT1–8 direct dispatch versus generic Down grouping by four. `iq_avx2.cpp:463-470` chooses gathered formats; `:477-487` exposes an IQ3_S-only paired GU experiment; `:517-525` dispatches it. `q2_avx2.cpp:49-88` describes Q2 bitplane transform and changes float reduction order; `q2_avx2_rows.inl:19-66` decodes Q2 blocks and splits NT>4 into groups of four. `expert_layout.cpp:133-177` gives worker/task machinery and affinity setup; `pool.cpp:481-504` runs native GU, intermediate activation quantization, Down and accumulates phase wall time.

## Exact work and packed extent for H=2560, FF=640

Each GU projection has 640 output rows and 10 weight blocks per row; both Gate and Up are evaluated. Each Down has 2,560 output rows and 20 blocks/row for 32-value blocks or 10 blocks/row for Q2_0's 64-value blocks. All rows consume the full inner dimension.

| phase / format | block values and bytes | blocks per output row | row count | logical packed bytes / expert | products per token / expert |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GU IQ2_S (type 22; two projections) | 256 / 82 B | 10 | 1,280 | 1,049,600 B | 3,276,800 |
| GU IQ3_XXS (type 18; two projections) | 256 / 98 B | 10 | 1,280 | 1,254,400 B | 3,276,800 |
| GU IQ3_S (type 21; two projections) | 256 / 110 B | 10 | 1,280 | 1,408,000 B | 3,276,800 |
| Down IQ4_NL (type 20) | 32 / 18 B | 20 | 2,560 | 921,600 B | 1,638,400 |
| Down Q2_0 (type 2 in GGML; native layer type 42 here) | 64 / 36 B | 10 | 2,560 | 921,600 B | 1,638,400 |

Thus per expert-token pair the listed combinations span 1,971,200–2,329,600 logical packed bytes, excluding any alignment and non-expert tensors. The extents are precisely the bytes addressed by the complete row loops. They are not cache-line fills, DRAM bytes, physical read traffic, or a guarantee each byte reaches DRAM each token.

For one selected layer/expert, logical activation inputs are much smaller: Q8_K GU input is 10×292 = 2,920 B/token, Q8_0 IQ4_NL Down input is 20×34 = 680 B/token. Q2_0 Down uses Strata's planar `ActQ`, not a GGML Q8_1 block: for FF=640 the live image carries 640 Q bytes, 20 scales, sums and hx values, plus the 640-byte bitplane image and 40 psum/pscale lanes, about 1,840 B of fields (excluding alignment/padding). The actual `ActQ` definition is `include/strata/kernels/cpu/expert.hpp:67-80`; its legacy function name does not denote the GGML block layout. GU activation quantization is once per routed token/layer before jobs (`expert_source.cpp` is detailed in R263); the intermediate FF activation is quantized once after GU and before Down. Those small vectors are read across many rows; whether they remain in L1/L2 is not determined by their logical size. The current request's `worker5/tasks18/cache144` is configuration context, not proof of six-way CPU service or any cache residency.

The multiply counts correspond to H×FF for Gate and Up, then FF×H for Down. Each product is conventionally 2 FLOPs, excluding decode, scaling/corrections, SiLU, quantization, reductions, and scheduling. Decode loops for IQ2_S/IQ3_XXS/IQ3_S cover 8 32-value halves per 256-value block: 51,200 halves per projection/expert and 102,400 halves across Gate+Up. IQ4_NL covers 51,200 32-weight blocks/Down expert; Q2_0 covers 25,600 64-weight blocks. These are loop iterations, not instruction counts.

At 70 tokens/s the fully cold logical routed top-10 expert extent given in the request would be 68.76 GB/s decimal, but that is not an estimate of physical RAM traffic. The corrected R369 v2 explicitly establishes that logical union bytes cannot prove memory-controller traffic or token-rate feasibility. Keep this as accounting only.

## Existing native path that a measurement must represent

The GGUF type traits determine activation format and block geometry. IQ GU uses Q8_K. IQ4_NL Down uses Q8_0. Q2_0 Down uses the local Q8_1 `ActQ` and AVX2/AVX-VNNI row kernels. On an AVX2 CPU without AVX-512, native IQ GU can take Strata's IQ AVX2 implementation at NT≥1 for most supported GU types; IQ2_XXS retains the configured default NT minimum 2 (`native_expert.cpp:94-112`). For this target, AVX-512 paths and SDE timing are irrelevant. Ryzen gather defaults should be tested as separate variants, not selected by a vendor-name rule.

The IQ GU multi-row loop decodes each weight half once per activation group and reuses its grid/sign/scale vectors for all NT tokens. Gate and Up remain separate row loops and decode their own weight matrices; repeated activation vectors may be cache-resident. IQ4_NL Down similarly unpacks nibbles, does its PSHUFB lookup, and makes |weight| once per block, then loops over tokens. Q2_0 Down unpacks codes once per block before the NT loop. Per-token integer multiply/add and float accumulation remain. This makes GU decode/issue pressure, activation quantization, Down, and scheduling all plausible costs; the source does not identify which controls end-to-end latency.

A source detail worth guarding in any A/B: `STRATA_Q2_BITPLANE` is enabled by default and adds an activation-side image pass; it changes Q2_0's float summation/reduction order (q2_avx2.cpp comments give an Intel benchmark, not 5600X evidence). Existing production correctness does not itself establish full 256K quality. Keep FP32 recurrence state untouched and keep the 256K quality qualification open.

## Priority: what to measure, then what might transfer

1. **Join phase time to real NT and format counts (first).** Existing `pool.cpp:491-502` already times GU, intermediate quantization, and Down as host-wall phases. A request-level delta can be captured from these counters without adding clocks inside worker loops. Pair it with the actual `(layer, GU type, Down type, nt)` job histogram; do not infer all jobs are NT1 or IQ3_S from the model label. Report per-request ms, distinct jobs, ΣNT, and buckets 1,2,3,4,5–8 separately. Interpret phase wall times as overlapping host work, not additive critical-path contributions when they overlap GPU activity. This is already close to the exact-service seam described in R173/R284; the delta here is to use it specifically to decide whether the newly identified NT>4 duplicate decode is exposed.
2. **Kernel-only matched cache-size arms.** Use the existing CPU parity bench's production dispatch (not a new model/GPU run) and the real format/geometry: NT1–4, plus NT5–8 for paths that permit those group sizes. Compare a compact expert set intentionally below L3 against a streaming set larger than L3, pinned workers and host participation matching the service config. Run GU, IQ4_NL Down, Q2_0 Down, and quantizer phases separately. This establishes hot-cache versus streaming service and whether decode/quant/Down dominates within the kernel; neither arm alone is a pure DRAM roof. Include per-thread CPU time/cycles and LLC misses if already available at low observer cost, and regard these as supporting counters rather than physical bytes. A hardware memory-controller counter is needed to claim measured DRAM traffic.
3. **Bounded NT5–8 Down reuse experiment (new source opportunity).** `iq_avx2_rows.inl:240-250`, `:320-330`, and `q2_avx2_rows.inl:54-66` split NT>4 into chunks of four, re-entering the full row/block loop for each chunk. Consequently each IQ4_NL nibble block or Q2_0 code block is decoded/unpacked twice for NT5–8, while NT1–4 decodes once. GU does not split this way: `:224-235` instantiates NT5,6,7,8 directly and its row decoder loops across all tokens. This is a source-visible asymmetry that the reviewed R263 candidates did not mention. First require a nontrivial real-route NT5–8 count and measurable Down phase contribution. Then prototype one row loop that loads/decodes a block once and processes activations in bounded groups of four before advancing; this retains a bounded register footprint without converting or storing a full floating weight row. Check compiler spill output, parity versus the current code and GGML, per-NT kernel timings, full-request timing and 256K state/quality gates before dispatching it. If NT5–8 is absent/rare, reject the implementation as immaterial.
4. **Per-format GU decode versus multiply test.** The existing format methods differ: IQ2_S's scalar path assembles 4 grid entries from spread indices and reads sign bytes; IQ3_XXS performs 8 byte-indexed grid reads plus sign lookup; IQ3_S builds spread indices and performs 8 grid reads. All also do integer dot/sign operations and per-block float accumulation. Existing gather variants are already known from source to be nontransferable: i7-14700/14900KF outcomes vary by type, and current Ryzen auto-selection stays scalar. Measure scalar and gathered arms for each type at the active NTs before any dispatch rule. No expected winning type or CPU speed is asserted.
5. **Quantization is likely small per operation but measure before optimizing.** Input Q8_K quantization runs once per routed token per layer, not once per expert; FF quantization occurs once per distinct job-token between GU and Down. Its bytes and operation count are much lower than the full row products, but it can surface on host critical path while workers park. Existing q8k AVX2 path is intended bit-equal to GGML; Q2 bitplane activation preparation is another pass for that specific Down kernel. Measure its separate pool phase before proposing vector changes or a precision trade.
6. **Thread splitting and memory as separate hypotheses.** Native work is divided into contiguous ranges of flattened `expert × output-row` (`pool.cpp:323-360`); 5600X has six physical cores and 12 logical CPUs per AMD spec. Task count 18 controls row fragments, while five workers plus caller participation and pinning determine active participants. Compare current five-worker/task18 setting with a small worker/task sweep only after phase evidence points to underfill, tail imbalance, or saturation. Avoid treating SMT count, task count, logical bytes, or nominal DDR rate as measured throughput. If hot-set and streaming arms have similar kernel service, DRAM is less likely to dominate; if streaming worsens, it still does not prove DRAM without controller events.

## External implementation scan and transfer boundary

Primary-source references consulted:
- llama.cpp/ggml CPU type traits connect IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, IQ2_S to Q8_K and IQ4_NL to Q8_0: [ggml-cpu.c](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c). Its x86 IQ kernels are the closest format-matched implementation reference: [ggml-cpu x86 sources](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/master/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86).
- [llama.cpp IQ2_XS optimization discussion](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/5152) describes moving scale construction into vector registers. This class of scale/index precomputation is already represented in Strata's AVX2 decoders; do not repeat it as a new proposal.
- [KTransformers AMX CPU MoE notes](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/ktransformers/blob/main/doc/en/AMX.md) explicitly design around cache hierarchy and in-place operation. Its cache-residency principle transfers as a measurement design (hot versus streaming), not its AMX kernel or Xeon result.
- A recent [KTransformers AVX2 MXFP4 kernel commit](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/ktransformers/commit/9481291) reports AVX2 LUT decode changes and caps large batch paths to bound per-thread FP32 staging; its MXFP4 format and dual EPYC timings do not transfer to these IQ formats or a 5600X. The useful question for Strata is register/spill growth and bounded tile width when sharing decode across multiple activations; the concrete NT>4 wrapper seam above comes from Strata's own source.
- [vLLM CPU installation and supported-model guidance](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/getting_started/installation/cpu.md) does not provide an IQ3_S/IQ2_S CPU MoE kernel that can be substituted here. SGLang's documented Expert Parallelism framework is dispatch/pre-permute/core/post-permute/combine for GPU-oriented backends, not a matching CPU IQ row-dot implementation: [SGLang EP documentation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/advanced_features/expert_parallelism.mdx).
- [Intel LLM Scaler](https://github.com/intel/llm-scaler) and [IPEX LLM inference notes](https://github.com/intel/intel-extension-for-pytorch/tree/main/examples/cpu/llm/inference) focus on Intel accelerator and AVX-512/AMX-oriented low-precision paths. No ISA-compatible IQ decoder for Ryzen AVX2 was identified in this scan. The general weight-only quantization concept is not itself a new transfer: this engine already consumes packed IQ and has AVX2 kernels. Do not transfer advertised or blog/reddit/commit-comment speedups to this target.
- The llama.cpp issue/discussion ecosystem contains MoE expert-cache ideas and user-reported speedups. Those address GPU residency/copy work rather than this CPU row kernel; cache-policy work is already out of this report's scope and is being researched separately.

The llama.cpp feature matrix currently labels IQ CPU AVX2 support, with IQ kernels slower than K-quants of comparable size in its context; this is a project-level warning that low bit count does not mean low decode cost. It is not a per-format or 5600X measurement. [llama.cpp feature matrix](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/wiki/Feature-matrix/c0eb5b983a4656b18b8c99c456684e30b4410672)

## Prior-report delta and known limits

- R263 already proposed IQ3_S gather, paired GU activation reuse, IQ4_NL NT1, and separated pool/kernel timing; those are not claimed as new. Fixed HEAD now contains a paired-GU opt-in and the gather machinery. R263's 5600X outcomes remained unmeasured.
- R224 already established that IQ2_S NT2 shares decode across tokens and noted register spills at NT4 in emitted code. Do not repeat multi-token amortization or NT4 spill inspection as a new insight.
- R83 already warned that IQ2_S NT1 custom path can differ in reduction order from GGML. No NT1 precision/dispatch change is recommended here.
- R173/R284 already specified pool phase/job instrumentation. This report's refinement is the exact NT5–8 Down duplicate-decode condition and format-specific row/byte accounting for selecting which phase deserves attention.
- R369v2 corrects logical route extent arithmetic and explicitly leaves overlap, cache hits, and DRAM bytes unmeasured. This report uses its boundary and makes no rate feasibility claim.
- Direct model measurement, sustained 256K quality, per-layer route/NT distribution, actual LLC/DRAM receipts, exact quantization cost, and any 5600X kernel-only comparison remain unobserved. These are decision inputs, not inferred results.

## Adoption gates

No precision or quantization change should be considered from this source analysis. Keep recurrence state FP32; 256K quality remains unqualified. Do not adopt a gather selector, paired GU path, new row tile, or worker/task setting until the exact type/NT cell shows a repeatable phase win, parity/greedy invariance passes, full request decode improves, and relevant 256K state/quality checks pass. Main's currently active phase-cache/sourceLLVM operation retains exclusive ownership of builds/tests/GPU and decides whether any follow-up is in scope.
